_comment: Tunable thresholds for the non-food findings, kept out of the code for the same
reason nutrient_policy.json is: these numbers encode judgement about what counts
as a genuine issue, and judgement should be reviewable and changeable without a
deploy. Every value here has a built-in default in domain_findings.py, so
deleting a key is safe and deleting the file is safe.

_why: The circular standard deviation of the time the user falls asleep. 60 min is
the point where a schedule stops being 'roughly the same time' — below it the
night-to-night variation is ordinary life, above it the body clock is being
asked to move, which shows up in deep sleep and next-day appetite.
Two strength sessions a week is the low end of what maintains muscle in a
calorie deficit; it is a floor, not a target. The gap rule is about naming a
pause while it is still a pause. `strength_types` matches against the free-text
workout_types column, so it carries both the API's English type names and the
Portuguese words the user might see.
Bioimpedance readings are hydration-noisy, so these compare half-window means
and use thresholds well clear of the day-to-day swing. 0.4 kg of lean mass and
0.4 percentage points of body fat are both roughly one SD of a fortnight's
readings — smaller moves than that are not signal.
min_days is higher than the module's MIN_DAYS because a body composition trend
genuinely needs a fortnight before it means anything.
bowel_movement is blank-means-no, so the rule only reads days that carry any
self-report at all: a stretch where the user stopped logging must not read as
constipation. min_logged_days is what enforces that. 0.6 (roughly 4 days in 7)
is the low end of normal frequency, not a medical threshold — the finding names
a pattern and pairs it with fibre, and says nothing clinical.
